```{r, Load libraries}

library(janitor)
```

```{r}
#| output: FALSE

# Load data
data<-read_excel("./Attachment_Anxiety_Data.xlsx")


# Inspect data
head(data)

unique(data$Relationship)
unique(data$Ethnicity)
```

```{r, clean data}
#| output: FALSE

# Use mutate to rename variables in a meaningful way (as stated in the README file) 
# Gender value: 1=male, 2=female 
# Age group: 1=18-24, 2=24-34, 3=35-44, 4=45-54, 5=55-64
# Relationship status value: 1=married, 2=in a relationship, 4=divorced, 5=in a relationship, 6=never, 7=prefer not to say
# Extract for variables: gender, age group, relationship status
# Mutate to convert AAD values to integers

AAD.clean <- data |>
    mutate(Gender = case_when(
      Gender==1 ~ "Male", 
      Gender==2 ~"Female", 
      TRUE ~ "NA")) |>
    mutate(`Age group` = case_when(
      `Age group`==1 ~ "18-24", 
      `Age group`==2 ~ "24-34",
      `Age group`==3 ~ "35-44", 
      `Age group`==4 ~ "45-54", 
      `Age group`==5 ~ "55-64", 
      TRUE ~ "NA")) |> 
  mutate(Relationship = case_when(
    Relationship==1 ~ "married", 
    Relationship==2 ~ "in a relationship", 
    Relationship==4 ~ "divorced", 
    Relationship==5 ~ "in a relationship",
    Relationship==6 ~ "never in a relationship", 
    Relationship==7 ~ "prefer not to say", 
    TRUE ~ "NA")) |> 
  select(Gender, `Age group`, Relationship,
           SA_1:SEst_10) |>
    mutate(across(SA_1:SEst_10, as.integer))

```

```{r, score items}
#| output: FALSE

# Answer key: which items belong to each subscale.
# "-" marks reverse-coded items (e.g., E1 "Don't talk a lot" -> high = LESS extraverted), which get flipped so higher scores always mean more of the trait. Done so seprately.

ans_key_A<- list(SA=c(
    "SA_1", "SA_2", "SA_3", "SA_4", "-SA_5", 
    "SA_6","SA_7","SA_8","-SA_9","SA_10",
    "-SA_11","SA_12", "SA_13","SA_14", "SA_15",
    "SA_16","SA_17", "SA_18","SA_19", "SA_20")) 
ans_key_B<- list(AA=c(
     "AA_1", "AA_2", "AA_3", "AA_4", "AA_5",
     "AA_6","AA_7","AA_8","AA_9"))
ans_key_C<- list(SEst=c(
      "SEst_1", "-SEst_2", "SEst_3", "SEst_4", "-SEst_5", 
    "-SEst_6","SEst_7","-SEst_8","-SEst_9", "SEst_10"))

# Average items per person, and compute Cronbach's alpha.
# Returns $scores (per-person scores as averages since we set totals to F) and $alpha (reliability)
scores_A<-scoreItems(
  ans_key_A, AAD.clean, totals = F, 
  min=0, max=4)
scores_B<-scoreItems(
  ans_key_B, AAD.clean, totals = F, 
  min=1, max=7)
scores_C<-scoreItems(
  ans_key_C, AAD.clean, totals = F, 
  min=1, max=4)

# Turn each key into a dataframe!
scores_A.df<-as.data.frame(scores_A$scores)
scores_B.df<-as.data.frame(scores_B$scores)
scores_C.df<-as.data.frame(scores_C$scores)

# Combine all scores into one datafram
tot_scores.df<- cbind(scores_A.df,scores_B.df, scores_C.df)

```

```{r, combine data frames}
#| output: FALSE

# Combine the original data set with the new scores dataframe
AAD.clean<-cbind(AAD.clean, tot_scores.df)

# Inspect new data set
head(AAD.clean)
```

```{r, reduced data}
#| output: FALSE

# Select only for the columns which you want to appear in your final data table
AAD.final<- AAD.clean |>
    select("Gender", "Age group", "Relationship", "SA", "AA", "SEst") |>
    mutate_if(is.numeric, round, 2) #round up or down decimal 
```

```{r, reproducible table for relationship distribution}
#| output: FALSE

# Create a demographics table of age group and relationship
demographic.table <- AAD.final |>
  tabyl(`Age group`, Relationship)

# Create your reproducible gt table
gttable.1 <- demographic.table |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(
    title = md("*Distribution of Age groups by Relationship Status*")
  )

```

```{r, reproducible table for attachment and anxiety scores}
#| output: FALSE

# Round Cronbach's alpha values to 2 decimal places.
alphas <- round(c(
  scores_A$alpha,
  scores_B$alpha,
  scores_C$alpha
), 2)

# Summary statistics for certain columns
summary <- describe(select(AAD.final, SA:SEst))
summary

# Label sample size for later in your reproducible document using describe
n <- (describe(AAD.final))[1,2]

# Name an object of Subscales so this can appear in your table
Subscales <- c("SA", "AA", "SEst")

# Create a column called Subscales in your summary table
summary$Subscales<- Subscales

# Select for only the columns which you want to appear in your final table
summary <- summary |>
    select(Subscales, mean, median, sd, range) |>
       mutate_if(is.numeric, round, 2)

# Combine summary information with alpha values
final.reptable <- cbind(summary, alphas)

# Create a reproducible table
gttable.2<- gt(final.reptable) |>
    tab_header(
        title = md("*Descriptive Statistics for Attachment and Social Anxiety*")) |>
    tab_stubhead(label= "Composites")|>
    tab_spanner(
        label="Central Tendency",
        columns = c(mean, median)
    )|>
        tab_spanner(
        label="Variability",
        columns = c(sd, range)
        )|>
            tab_spanner(
        label="Reliability Values (Chronbach's alpha)",
        columns = c(alphas)
            ) 

```

```{r, filtered dataset}
#| output: FALSE

# Use filter to extract only those participants who are over 18 and under 65

AAD.filtered <- AAD.clean |>
    filter(`Age group` >= 18 & `Age group` <= 64)
# Checking that age restriction worked
table(AAD.filtered$`Age group`)

# Filter to extract only those participants who are in a relationship, divorced, or married (Use in next step)
AAD.filtered <- AAD.filtered |>
    filter(Relationship =="in a relationship")
# Checking that age restriction worked
table(AAD.filtered$Relationship)
 
```

```{r, reproducible FILTERED table for attachment anxiety scores}
#| output: FALSE

# Round Cronbach's alpha values to 2 decimal places. t transposes the data, which is not needed with the other data set. Follow code in instruction document.
alphas_filtered <- round(c(
  scores_A$alpha,
  scores_B$alpha,
  scores_C$alpha
), 2)

# Summary statistics for certain columns
summary_filtered <- describe(select(AAD.filtered, SA:SEst))
summary_filtered

# Name an object of Subscales so this can appear in your table
Subscales <- c("SA", "AA", "SEst")

#Create a column called Subscales in your summary table
summary_filtered$Subscales<- Subscales

# Select for only the columns which you want to appear in your final table
summary_filtered <- summary_filtered |>
    select(Subscales, mean, median, sd, range) |>
       mutate_if(is.numeric, round, 2)

# Combine summary information with alpha values
filtered.reptable <- cbind(summary_filtered, alphas_filtered)

# Create a reproducible table
gttable.3<- gt(filtered.reptable) |>
    tab_header(

        columns = c(mean, median)
    )|>
        tab_spanner(
        label="Variability",
        columns = c(sd, range)
        )|>

            ) 
```

## Intro

## Methods

### Participants

In this data set there were `{r} n` participants, with varying distributions of education type (Table 1).

`{r} gttable.1`

### Measures

In this Attachment and Social Anxiety data set, the 3 factors refer to the 3 composites included in the Attachment Anxiety Data. Experiences in Close Relationships (Cronbach's alpha = `{r} alphas[1]`). Social Interaction Anxiety Scale (Cronbach's alpha = `{r} alphas[2]`). and Rosenberg Self-Esteem Scale (Cronbach's alpha = `{r} alphas[3]`).

### Data Analysis Strategy

The data for variables SA_1, AA_1, SEst_1, were reverse keyed.

## Results

`{r} gttable.2`
In this AAD data set, the 3 factors refer to the 3 composites included in the Attachment Anxiety Data.
Participants had a mean score on Experiences in Close Relationships of `{r} final.reptable[1,2]`, on Social Interaction Anxiety Scale of `{r} final.reptable[2,2]`, on Rosenberg Self-Esteem Scale of `{r} final.reptable[3,2]`.

`{r} gttable.3`
When only including participants over age 18 and below age 65 in a relationship, this AAD data set, the 3 factors refer to the 3 composites included in the Attachment Anxiety Data. Participants had a mean score on Experiences in Close Relationships of `{r} filtered.reptable[1,2]`, on Social Interaction Anxiety Scale of `{r} filtered.reptable[2,2]`, on Rosenberg Self-Esteem Scale of `{r} filtered.reptable[3,2]`.
